one_sentence_failure_summary: The initial CSS expression() regex did not handle nested parentheses, leaving a broken `.b { width: ); }` artifact in the sanitized file, and subsequent fixes (though functionally correct on fresh input) were never validated against the actual test suite before the agent claimed completion.
t_err_evidence: Step 13 introduces the first style-block sanitizer using `re.sub(br'(?i)expression\s*\([^)]*\)\)?', b'', c)`. This regex uses `[^)]*` which cannot match past the first `)` in nested calls like `expression(alert('x'))`, so it strips only `expression(alert('x'` and leaves the trailing `)` behind, creating the `.b { width: ); }` artifact first observed in step 15.

True` meaning the sanitizer is now idempotent on the already-corrupted file. t_surface_evidence: Step 15 output shows line 7 as `.b { width: ); }` in /tmp/test3.html — the first observable sign that the expression() removal was incorrect and left a broken CSS artifact.
trigger_explanation: The agent's CSS expression regex `[^)]*` correctly targets parentheses but fails to handle nested parentheses in `expression(alert('x'))`. The outer `)` that closes `expression(...)` is consumed by the greedy stop at the first `)` (the one inside `alert('x')`), so the outer closing `)` is left behind. This is a regex design limitation — the agent lacked awareness that the CSS expression body could itself contain function calls with parentheses.
forewarning_evidence: Step 15 clearly shows `.b { width: ); }` — a broken CSS artifact demonstrating the expression() removal was incomplete. Despite multiple subsequent fix attempts (steps 16, 18, 20, 22), end-to-end testing at steps 17, 19, 23, and 28 consistently reproduced the same broken artifact.
